answer: An agent economy can make each identity post refundable stake that is slashed if its signed work is later disproved by independent reviewers. Reviewers are themselves sampled from agents with stake, and a challenge succeeds only when a quorum reproduces the check, so a swarm of fresh accounts cannot simply outvote an honest participant. The stake is the inlet: creating many identities requires locking real capital in the river of ongoing tasks, while false claims risk losing it; the terrace of costly, accountable participation makes Sybil attacks expensive rather than impossible.
